fact: Delhi is home to the Red Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
Mumbai is home to Bollywood, the largest film industry in the world in terms of films produced.
Kolkata was the capital of British India until 1911 and is known as the 'City of Joy'.
Chennai's Marina Beach is the second-longest urban beach in the world.
Bengaluru is called the 'Silicon Valley of India' for its IT hub status.
Hyderabad is famous for the Charminar and its world-renowned Hyderabadi biryani.
Jaipur is known as the 'Pink City' due to its distinct pink-colored buildings.
Varanasi is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Amritsar houses the Golden Temple, the holiest shrine in Sikhism.
Ahmedabad is home to Sabarmati Ashram, closely associated with Mahatma Gandhi.
Lucknow is called the 'City of Nawabs' for its Mughal and Awadhi heritage.
Pune is called the 'Oxford of the East' due to its educational institutions.
Mysuru Palace is lit with nearly 100,000 lights during Dussehra celebrations.
Agra is home to the Taj Mahal, one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
Shillong is nicknamed the 'Scotland of the East' for its natural beauty.
Leh, in Ladakh, is one of the highest permanently inhabited places in the world.
Udaipur is called the 'City of Lakes' for its many beautiful lakes.
Rishikesh is known as the 'Yoga Capital of the World'.
Bhopal is called the 'City of Lakes' for its natural and artificial lakes.
Kochi was once an important spice trading center with Arab and European merchants.
Darjeeling is famous for its tea and the Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Chandigarh is India’s first planned city, designed by Le Corbusier.
Guwahati houses the Kamakhya Temple, one of India’s most important Shakti Peethas.
Jodhpur is known as the 'Blue City' because of its indigo-colored houses.
Madurai is famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple with its colorful gopurams.
Patna, formerly Pataliputra, was a major capital in ancient India.
The Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram is considered the richest temple in the world.
Gwalior Fort is known as the 'Gibraltar of India'.
Nagpur is called the 'Orange City' for its high-quality oranges.
Indore has been ranked India’s cleanest city multiple times in a row.
Jamshedpur is India’s first planned industrial city, founded by Jamshedji Tata.
Surat is known as the 'Diamond City of India' for its diamond cutting and polishing industry.
Coimbatore is called the 'Manchester of South India' for its textile industry.
Kanpur was once the largest center of leather and textile industries in India.
Raipur is known as the 'Steel City of Central India'.
Dehradun is home to the Indian Military Academy.
Haridwar is one of the seven holiest Hindu cities and hosts the Kumbh Mela.
Ajmer is famous for the Ajmer Sharif Dargah of Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti.
Puri is famous for the Jagannath Temple and its annual Rath Yatra.
Bhubaneswar is called the 'Temple City of India' for its many ancient temples.
Srinagar is known for its Dal Lake and houseboats.
Manali is one of India’s most popular hill stations and adventure hubs.
Shimla was the summer capital of British India.
